- Avoid overreacting to recent sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot after positive sentiment, especially in early days of forecast horizon.
- Underweight sentiment when it’s mixed or negative; model often ignores negative sentiment signals, leading to overestimation of price.
- Apply mean reversion bias correction: if forecast is >20% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 15–30% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day forecasts, cap extreme outliers (e.g., >3x recent high or <0.5x recent low) unless sentiment is bullish and volatility is high.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), reduce forecast by 10–20% to avoid “sentiment blind spot” bias.
- Lag correction: if forecast is significantly higher than 14-day moving average, subtract 10–25% to account for delayed market reaction.
- Avoid forecasting sharp drops after recent spikes — model often predicts “rebound” instead of “reversal” when sentiment turns negative.
